title_vi: Mười tám mẫu thiết kế của nguồn: mười bốn mẫu, tìm trong thư viện chuẩn của Python

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a git fetch of the pinned commit and hashed as a Git blob; computed OID matches the source map. Non-empty source was read; no source-image bytes used.

claims.evidence: Behaviour of the standard-library examples checked by small Python 3.13.16 programs run on 2026-10-19 (adapter, composite, decorator, facade, flyweight, proxy, command-like, iterator, memento, observer-like, visitor); three timings/memory figures measured in three runs. Pattern definitions are the source's nicknames plus the author's one-line gloss, unchecked against the original book. Abstract Factory, Bridge and Mediator: no confident standard-library example found.

mobile.evidence: Figure drawn by scripts/figures (viewBox width 320, smallest font 15 px, shown at 13.5 px at 320 px); python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser passed; the lesson (Markdown to HTML, optional sections open, 16 px side gutters) rendered in Chromium at 320, 375 and 430 px with no horizontal overflow of the page, any table or any code block. Not learner testing and not GitHub or a real phone.

claims.claim_vi: Python 3.13.16 checks: io.TextIOWrapper reads a binary stream as text; functools.wraps keeps the name and sets __wrapped__; any object with __iter__/__next__ is an iterator; random.getstate/setstate restores the generator; ast.NodeVisitor dispatches visit_<Class> (4 names counted in 'a = b + c * d'); ElementTree elements form a tree iterated as a, b, c; weakref.proxy forwards access and raises ReferenceError after the object is gone; small ints up to 256 are shared and sys.intern shares equal strings; shutil.make_archive produces a zip in one call; functools.partial(pow, 2, 10)() gives 1024; weakref.finalize runs its callback once.
claims.section: io, functools, weakref, shutil, ast, random, xml.etree.ElementTree
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19 on Python 3.13.16.

claims.claim_vi: Costs, best of seven repeats x 1,000,000 calls, three runs: plain call 42-53 ns vs 102-105 ns wrapped by one decorator; o.v 25-26 ns vs weakref.proxy(o).v 38-40 ns; 1,000,000 strings with 1,000 distinct values took 53.3 million bytes when built separately and 8.5 million bytes when shared through a dict (tracemalloc), identical in all three runs.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19; absolute numbers belong to the test machine.

claims.claim_vi: The source lists eighteen patterns with a nickname each: Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype, Singleton, Adapter, Bridge, Composite, Decorator, Facade, Flyweight, Proxy, Chain of Responsibility, Command, Iterator, Mediator, Memento, Observer, Visitor.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Meaning of each pattern: only the source's nickname plus the author's one-line gloss; not checked against the original design patterns book (not accessible).
claims.verified_by: Unchecked: general knowledge of the author; stated as such in the lesson.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: mười bốn mẫu chia ba kết quả, ba phép đo, giới hạn.
source_deviations: The source is a picture with eighteen nicknames; the lesson keeps fourteen (the other four - Builder, Prototype, Singleton, Chain of Responsibility - are not covered here), looks each up in the Python standard library, labels three as not found and two as approximate.
The lesson adds experiments the source does not contain.
